channel.title: Updated · all tabs
channel.description: Daily news and research, explained: every tab

item.title: FDA approves durvalumab plus enfortumab vedotin around surgery for bladder cancer patients who cannot take cisplatin
item.description: The FDA approved an immunotherapy plus antibody-drug conjugate given before and after bladder removal for patients who cannot or will not take cisplatin, after a 695-patient trial showed longer event-free and overall survival. (FDA, The ASCO Post)

item.title: US measles deaths climb as the CDC's tally reaches six and states report ten, with cases above 5,400
item.description: The CDC now counts six US measles deaths in 2026 while state health departments report ten, cases have reached 5,412, and a regional health body is weighing whether the US has lost measles-elimination status. (CIDRAP, PolitiFact)

item.title: China approves Lilly's orforglipron, the first GLP-1 weight-loss pill cleared there
item.description: China's drug regulator approved Eli Lilly's orforglipron tablets for adults with obesity, or overweight plus a related condition, making it the first oral GLP-1 drug for weight management in the country. (Pharmaceutical Technology, Plataforma Media)

item.title: Prehospital Extracorporeal Life Support in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
item.description: In a non-randomized Dutch study of 231 young adults in refractory cardiac arrest, helicopter teams starting ECMO on scene saw 40% survive to discharge versus 20% with conventional care. (Dinis Reis Miranda Xavier Moors Samir Ali Iscander M. Maissan Hans L. van Schuppen Lars Mommers Ellen E.M. Weelink Robert-Jan Houmes Fabian O. Kooij Marijn Tacken Manfred J. item.title: An LHX2-DACH1 regulatory innovation drives basal progenitor expansion in the primate neocortex
item.description: A small DNA switch that controls the gene DACH1, with a feature shared among primates, helps the developing cortex make more of a special stem cell abundant in primate brains, in organoids and mice. (Pei-Shan Hou, Ching-Yu Chuang, Feng-Lan Chiu et al. · National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University; Academia Sinica; Kyoto University)

item.title: A multi-tissue atlas of genetic regulatory effects in sheep
item.description: SheepGTEx maps how DNA variants control gene activity across 51 sheep tissues and cell types, and ancient DNA shows breeding favored variants acting in just one or a few tissues, such as skin. (Mian Gong, Ziyang Zhuang, Xiangrong Sun et al. · Aarhus University)

item.title: Climate Action Tracker finds the warming outlook has stalled for a fifth year, with current policies heading for 2.7°C
item.description: The Climate Action Tracker's COP31 update projects 2.7°C of warming by 2100 under current policies and says even full delivery of every pledge would permanently overshoot 1.5°C. (Climate Action Tracker, Ars Technica (Inside Climate News), The New York Times)

item.title: Atmospheric O2 reveals a strengthening ocean carbon sink and a stagnant net land sink since 1990
item.description: Three decades of precise air-oxygen measurements show the ocean has absorbed a growing share of fossil carbon since 1990, while the net land sink has not grown, contrary to many models. (Eric J. Morgan, Yuming Jin, Elena Kozlova et al. · Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego)

item.title: Carbon dioxide and amorphous water ices in the debris disk around β Pictoris
item.description: Webb detects glassy water ice mixed with carbon dioxide across the Beta Pictoris debris disk, a mixture that looks like comet ice formed in interstellar space before the star's planets. (S. K. Betti, C. H. Chen, C. Xie et al. · Space Telescope Science Institute)

item.title: Discovery of a likely supermassive neutron star in a remarkably wide binary
item.description: A red giant wobbling around an unseen companion of about 2.2 solar masses points to an unusually heavy neutron star in a wide, nearly circular orbit that standard binary models fail to produce. (Xinlin Zhao, Song Wang, Guang-Yao Xiao et al.)

item.title: US producer prices rise 6.5% over the year to October, the biggest annual gain since 2022, as inflation spreads beyond energy
item.description: US producer prices rose 0.3% in October, slightly less than forecast, but 6.5% over twelve months, the largest annual gain since November 2022, with food and core goods prices climbing. (The Globe and Mail (Reuters), The Jolt Journal)

item.title: The Fed's financial stability report finds AI is now the most-cited risk, named by 87% of surveyed market contacts
item.description: The Fed's twice-yearly stability report says AI enthusiasm keeps asset prices near historic highs, AI-related debt issuance has passed $680 billion this year, and 87% of surveyed contacts now see AI as a key risk. (Federal Reserve, Yahoo Finance)

item.title: Alberta cuts royalties on new oil sands projects to 2% for five years in a bid to double crude output
item.description: Alberta's new Oil Sands Growth Program guarantees eligible new projects a 10-year royalty schedule starting at 2%, part of Premier Danielle Smith's push to double oil production to eight million barrels a day. (Government of Alberta, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: An arbitrator imposes the first binding union contract for Amazon workers in North America, at a B.C. warehouse
item.description: About 800 workers at Amazon's YVR2 warehouse in Delta, B.C., are now covered by a three-year contract set by an arbitrator, with wages rising to $29 an hour; Amazon says it may go to court. (Unifor, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: TaskNet: Building Occupational Task Inventories from Worker Interviews at Scale
item.description: Researchers used system-run interviews with 132 workers to build task lists for six occupations, capturing 79 tasks missing from the O*NET occupational database and shifting estimates of AI exposure. (Jennifer Wang, Andreas Haupt, Isaac Robinson et al.)

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so its Dots agents can buy things for users, with approval for each purchase
item.description: OpenAI's new ChatGPT Wallet lets its Dots agents complete purchases with a tokenized card after the user approves each one biometrically, starting with a limited group of US Pro subscribers. (TechCrunch, The Verge)

item.title: llama.cpp and ggml reach version 1.0, promising stable interfaces for the local AI software built on them
item.description: The llama.cpp team released its libraries as v1.0.0 and adopted semantic versioning, so future breaking API or ABI changes will come only with major version bumps. (Hugging Face (ggml-org))

item.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
item.description: In a compute-matched study trained entirely from scratch, a pretrained vision encoder brings no advantage, but vision-only parameters do, and they work as well placed inside the first layers of the language backbone. (Ellis Brown, Chris Hoang, Shengyi Qian et al. · New York University, Meta FAIR)

item.title: Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space
item.description: PixVid fine-tunes a pretrained latent video diffusion model to generate every frame directly in pixels, matching its quality while enabling higher resolution, frame-accurate editing and one-frame control latency. (Yanke Song, Shuo Chen, Chris Rockwell et al. · Roblox, University of California, Merced)

item.title: Shaping Useful Noise: Energy Distributions Predict Visual Pretraining Quality
item.description: Synthetic image datasets train better representations when they cover the full range of likelihood levels real images occupy, and a simple distance over that "energy profile" predicts pretraining quality better than FID. (Ching Lam Choi, Antonio Torralba, Phillip Isola et al. · MIT CSAIL, Technical University of Munich)

item.title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
item.description: A reasoning model that edits another model's weights directly, without gradients, raised Qwen3.5-0.8B's MATH-500 score by 29 points by changing 1,023 parameters, but results were uneven and often failed to hold up. (Junru Hu, Cheng Tang, Wei Li et al.)

item.title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
item.description: A 47,000-hour study of how to train world action models finds that detailed captions and mixing human egocentric video with handheld-gripper demonstrations best preserve video-model knowledge while learning robot control. (Yu Zhou, Xinyuan Xia, Xuankun Yang et al. · Shanghai Jiao Tong University)

item.title: Attackers break into unpatched Check Point gateways through PHP2Shell and wipe servers at some Israeli organizations
item.description: Check Point says an attacker used the PHP2Shell flaws and a new privilege-escalation bug to take over unpatched Security Gateways, then wiped VMware ESXi servers at some Israeli organizations. (Check Point Research, BleepingComputer)

item.title: A failure in aging air traffic telecom equipment grounds every US departure for more than four hours
item.description: The FAA halted all US departures on Friday after legacy telecom switches and routers in the air traffic network started passing inconsistent data; officials linked the failure to patches made during an upgrade. (The Verge, WIRED, Ars Technica, Engadget)

item.title: Trezor confirms spy implants in three Safe 5 hardware wallets sold by a Southeast Asian reseller
item.description: Trezor found extra circuit boards in three Safe 5 wallets bought from reseller CryptoBilis that capture recovery phrases from the screen and send them out over a cellular network; new firmware blocks them. (BleepingComputer, Trezor)

item.title: Starship reaches orbit and deploys 26 Starlink satellites, but its booster diverts into the Gulf instead of a tower catch
item.description: SpaceX's 15th Starship flight put 26 Starlink V3 satellites into orbit, but the Super Heavy booster was diverted into the Gulf and exploded; a first attempt to catch the upper stage could come Saturday. (Ars Technica, Next Spaceflight)

item.title: Lessons Not Learned: Why Cross-Chain Bridges Keep Losing Billions the Same Way
item.description: Most cross-chain bridge losses since 2023 came from how bridges were set up, not from code bugs; a rubric scored from on-chain data, plus rate limits and emergency stops, would have cut modeled losses 105-fold. (Mohsen Ahmadvand, Piotr Dobaczewski, Camille Bouzerand · Monad Foundation)

item.title: The American Cancer Society now recommends regular PSA screening for prostate cancer, every two years from age 50
item.description: The American Cancer Society's new guideline recommends a PSA blood test every two years for average-risk men aged 50 to 69, and yearly from 45 for Black men and men with strong family history. (American Cancer Society, The New York Times)

item.title: FDA approves pimicotinib, a once-daily pill, for joint tumors that are hard to remove surgically
item.description: The FDA approved EMD Serono's pimicotinib for symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor after a placebo-controlled trial in which 56% of treated patients responded, against 3.2% on placebo. (FDA, HMP Global Oncology)

item.title: Intismeran Autogene plus Pembrolizumab for Resected Stage IIB to IV Melanoma
item.description: In a phase 3 trial of 1,137 people with resected high-risk melanoma, adding a personalized mRNA therapy to pembrolizumab raised two-year recurrence-free survival from 70.0% to 82.2%. (Georgina V. Long Muhammad A. Khattak Helen J. Gogas Dirk Schadendorf Ana Arance Matteo S. Carlino Piotr Rutkowski Gareth Rivalland Antoni Ribas Janice M. Mehnert Patrick A. item.title: Cross-species multiomic atlas of the primate basal ganglia
item.description: A cell-by-cell atlas of 1.8 million nuclei from human, macaque and marmoset basal ganglia finds 61 cell types conserved over 76 million years and maps psychiatric and neurodegenerative risk onto specific cells. (Nelson J. Johansen, Yuanyuan Fu, Matthew Schmitz et al. · Allen Institute)

item.title: Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA
item.description: In mice, the gut antibody IgA slows the renewal of the colon lining through a surface protein called DMBT1, and its absence raises susceptibility to colorectal tumors. (Gregory P. Donaldson, Gabriella Lima dos Reis, Marwa Saad et al. · The Rockefeller University)

item.title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
item.description: An independent imaging method built only on calibration-proof measurements recovers the ring around M87's black hole, 42.2 microarcseconds across, implying a mass of about 6.5 billion Suns. (Samuel Lai, Nithyanandan Thyagarajan, O. Ivy Wong et al.)

item.title: Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks
item.description: A newly found 3.95-billion-year-old rock in North China formed from ocean crust buried to mantle depths, suggesting a short-lived subduction event early in Earth's history. (Hangqiang Xie, Chunyan Dong, Pengchuan Li et al.)

item.title: Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines
item.description: Tidal turbine blades made of flexible rubber matched the energy yield of rigid blades with active pitch control while cutting fatigue-causing load swings by up to a third. (Zhehong Zhang, Junchen Tan, Eric-Carin Neba et al.)

item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia's CEO, CFO Colette Kress takes over on an interim basis, and the shares open down more than 13%
item.description: Nvidia's co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and director with immediate effect; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while the board searches for a successor, and Huang has agreed to testify to Congress. (TechCrunch, BBC, TechCrunch)

item.title: The Fed scraps its October 2027 rate vote and holds no December meeting, so no rate decision is due between mid-November 2027 and late January 2028
item.description: The Fed's revised 2027 calendar keeps eight meetings but turns October's into a strategy session with no rate decision and drops December, part of Chair Kevin Warsh's plan to meet less often. (Federal Reserve, The New York Times)

item.title: US existing-home sales fall 5.5% in October to 3.75 million, the lowest pace since August 2010, as mortgage rates climb
item.description: Sales of previously owned US homes fell 5.5% in October to an annual pace of 3.75 million, down 8.8% from a year earlier, as 30-year mortgage rates hover near 7.18%. (National Association of Realtors, The Guardian)

item.title: Cisco raises its annual revenue forecast to as much as $75.8 billion after a record quarter driven by AI networking
item.description: Cisco's quarterly revenue rose 24% to a record $18.5 billion, beating estimates, and it lifted its fiscal 2027 outlook and its forecast for AI infrastructure sales to cloud giants to $9 billion. (Cisco, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Clearing the Fog: Price Transparency, Market Churn, and Consumer Welfare in Short-Term Rentals
item.description: After California required Airbnb and similar hosts to show fee-inclusive prices, guests became more price-sensitive, nightly rates rose 4.8%, and many fee-heavy listings left the market, with net gains for consumers on average. (Ginger Zhe Jin, Liad Wagman, Jingyi Xing)

item.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast Gemini 4 model that replaces 3.8 Flash and now powers Search
item.description: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast, cheaper Gemini 4 model priced at $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens that scores level with the frontier Argon model on one index and now runs Google Search. (Google DeepMind, Ars Technica, TechCrunch)

item.title: Nonprofits sue OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceX to halt frontier AI development
item.description: Four nonprofits asked a San Francisco court to stop five leading AI developers from building or deploying new models, citing the companies' own warnings of catastrophic risk under California unfair-competition law. (Associated Press via BNN Bloomberg, Reuters via Claims Journal)

item.title: Goal Encoding in LLMs
item.description: A sparse set of attention heads in a coding LLM encodes the next sub-goal before it is written, can be read out in plain English, and steers behavior across programming languages. (Arnab Sen Sharma, Eric Todd, Sheridan Feucht et al. · Northeastern University, Parallax, University of Copenhagen)

item.title: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies
item.description: Memory-augmented robot policies often track elapsed time rather than events, so a harmless pause makes them believe work was done; indexing memory by events recovers much of the loss. (Chubin Zhang, Bo An · Nanyang Technological University)

item.title: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP
item.description: FOAM keeps nearly all of the SOAP optimizer's quality in LLM pre-training while using half its optimizer memory and reaching AdamW's final loss in about AdamW's own wall-clock time. (Jaemyung Yu, Byeongho Heo, Sangdoo Yun et al. · NAVER AI Lab)

item.title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
item.description: Tree-Ising fixes a small reasoning model's endless loops by flipping signs and shifting exponents in its stored weights, beating a frontier-agent repair on math benchmarks at about $0.90 instead of $312. (Hadi Salloum, Ammar Ali)

item.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
item.description: Decision models that act poorly can still teach well: asked in hindsight whether each action helped, JEV lifts a 1.5B agent's ALFWorld success from 72.8% to 82.9% over outcome-only GRPO. (Haochen Liu, Qianhao Zhu, Zixuan Wang et al. · Zhejiang University, Baidu Inc.)

item.title: A Microsoft 365 outage tied to Exchange Online knocks out email, Teams and Copilot for more than 12 hours
item.description: Microsoft 365 services that depend on Exchange Online failed worldwide from Thursday afternoon, and Microsoft's fixes had not brought sustained recovery more than 12 hours later. (BleepingComputer, The Register)

item.title: Apache patches a critical HTTP/2 flaw in its web server that could let attackers run code remotely
item.description: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 fixes a critical race condition in its HTTP/2 module that could let an unauthenticated attacker run code on servers that have HTTP/2 switched on. (Apache HTTP Server Project, BleepingComputer)

item.title: Police in nine countries seize 235 servers behind the Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC malware
item.description: An Operation Endgame action coordinated by Europol took down 235 servers and 257 domains used by three malware families and found about 6.4 million stolen credentials. (BleepingComputer, The Record)

item.title: Google opens pre-orders for its first Gemini smart glasses, made with Warby Parker, Gentle Monster and Samsung
item.description: Google's camera-equipped "intelligent eyewear," starting at $395, is up for pre-order ahead of a December 10 launch, with privacy limits such as a tamper-checked recording light. (Google, Ars Technica)

item.title: A Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Architecture with Globally Driven Atom Arrays
item.description: A design for neutral-atom quantum computers that picks which qubits to operate on by moving helper atoms, letting simple global laser and microwave pulses run error-corrected computation in simulation. (Zhihao Zhang, Shuaifan Cao, Xinyang Yu et al. · Fudan University)

item.title: Beam's base-edited sickle cell therapy keeps patients free of severe pain crises for a year in its pivotal trial
item.description: Beam Therapeutics says its one-time base-edited cell therapy, risto-cel, met its main goal of 12 months without severe pain crises in a 49-patient single-arm trial, and plans a US filing. (PharmaShots (summary of Beam's press release), BioPharm International)

item.title: A Lancet Psychiatry analysis compares how well 21 antidepressants keep depression at bay over months to years
item.description: Pooling 115 studies longer than 12 weeks, researchers found escitalopram, duloxetine and agomelatine somewhat more likely than fluoxetine to bring lasting improvement; experts call the differences modest. (The New York Times, BBC News)

item.title: Everyone in a 100,000-person All of Us sample carries gene variants that affect medicines, and a quarter got an affected drug
item.description: A Pitt-led analysis of nearly 100,000 genomes found every participant carried at least one drug-relevant variant (median nine), 24.4% had been prescribed an affected drug, and over 17,000 variants were new. (University of Pittsburgh via Medical Xpress, STAT, Science Translational Medicine)

item.title: UNC13A splice correction rescues synaptic dysfunction induced by TDP-43 loss
item.description: In lab-grown human neurons lacking the ALS protein TDP-43, fixing one splicing error in the synapse gene UNC13A with an antisense drug restored communication between neurons. (Matthew J. Keuss, Peter Harley, Eugeni Ryadnov et al. · King's College London; University College London; Francis Crick Institute; Leibniz-FMP; Trace Neuroscience)

item.title: Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia
item.description: Yearly stored blood samples show that in two-thirds of women who later got acute myeloid leukaemia, the first driver mutation arose before age 20, and mutant clones then grew predictably. (Caroline J. Watson, Gladys Y. P. Poon, Hamish A. J. MacGregor et al. · University of Cambridge; University College London)

item.title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
item.description: GPS-tracked tapirs and giant anteaters in Brazil carried more microplastics in their blood when their home ranges held more human disturbance or lay nearer waste facilities. (Marcia de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz, Arnaud L. J. Desbiez, Mario Henrique Alves et al. · University of British Columbia (Kelowna); Center for Advanced Systems Understanding (CASUS), Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf)

item.title: Euclid's first major data release maps more than 900 million galaxies and about 15,000 likely gravitational lenses
item.description: ESA's Euclid telescope has published its first major data release, covering about 14% of its planned survey, with over 900 million galaxies, 60 million possible quasars and roughly 15,000 probable strong lenses. (The Guardian, ESA Euclid)

item.title: ESA's Hera begins close-up study of the asteroid pair NASA's DART mission hit in 2022
item.description: ESA says its Hera spacecraft is now studying the asteroid Didymos and its moonlet Dimorphos from 25 to 30 kilometres away, starting a "crash site investigation" of the first asteroid deflection test. (Phys.org (Associated Press), ESA)
